section: Stress and Nicotine on Nutrition and Chronic Diseases
text:
Stress and Nicotine on Nutrition and Chronic Diseases
Effects of Stress and Nicotine on Nutrition

The aim of this systematic review was to explore the impacts of stress and nicotine products on nutrition and chronic diseases in individuals aged 18–25, with a particular focus on college students. Their correlation with psychological health, physical health, and various lifestyle factors had become a critical area of study. Stress was strongly correlated with nicotine use, particularly in young adults experiencing heightened levels of stress. Reports from organizations such as the National Institute on Drug Abuse (NIDA) and the National Institutes of Health (NIH) showed the growing trend of vaping among this population.

title: Experience
text:
Gwinnett United in Drug Education (GUIDE), Inc.



Lawrenceville, GA; Waleska, GA



Conducted research and took certification-based trainings related to Reducing Access to Lethal Means (among youths and adults) and on other topics. Findings were presented to the community (i.e., coalition boards, parents, and businesses).
Project included creating a booklet (with related resources) along with a presentation based on the steps and findings regarding Reducing Access to Lethal Means among youths and adults. The main topics included firearm, suffocation, and poisoning safety.

Utilized the Canva visual workspace platform to develop a website (https://gwinnettandsurroundingareaschri.my.canva.site/), with help from organizations in Gwinnett and surrounding areas, to provide resources related to harm reduction, mental health services, advocacy, and other categories to community members.

title: About
text:
I am a developing public health professional committed to advancing health equity through prevention, communication, and community-centered program management. My aspiration include designing, leading, and evaluating programs that reduce preventable harms, especially suicide, chronic disease, and inequities affecting underserved communities.
My past and current work combines and shows creativity, research, and leadership, from developing resource directories and educational materials to understanding why health problems occur and creating solutions that will empower communities. I believe my interests (in communication, behavioral health, and artistic projects) and past experiences (e.g., R.A.L.M research, resource website, and thesis on stress or nicotine from my undergraduate thesis) demonstrate my goal and reasons.
